readings.title: Shelomoh's Blessing and Dedication Sacrifices
readings.subtitle: The fourteen-day festival concludes with the people returning home joyful.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 8:54] And it came to be, when Shelomoh had ended praying all this prayer and supplication to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that he rose up from before the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread up to the heavens.
[55] And he stood and blessed <dn>את</dn> all the assembly of Yisra’ěl with a loud voice, saying,
[56] “Blessed be <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who has given rest to <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl, according to all that <dn>He</dn> promised. There has not failed one word of all <dn>His</dn> good word, which <dn>He</dn> promised through <dn>His</dn> servant Mosheh.
[57] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> is with us as <dn>He</dn> was with our fathers – <dn>He</dn> does not leave us nor forsake us –
[58] to incline our hearts to <dn>Himself</dn>, to walk in all <dn>His</dn> ways, and to guard <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, which <dn>He</dn> commanded our fathers.
[59] “And let these words of mine, with which I have made supplication before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, be near <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn> day and night, to maintain the cause of <dn>His</dn> servant and the cause of <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl, the matter of each day in its day,
[60] so that all the peoples of the earth might know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>, there is no one else.
[61] “Let your heart therefore be perfect to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> laws and guard <dn>His</dn> commands, as at this day.”
[62] And the sovereign and all Yisra’ěl with him slaughtered <dn>את</dn> slaughterings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[63] And Shelomoh slaughtered <dn>את</dn> slaughterings of peace offerings, which he slaughtered to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the sovereign and all the children of Yisra’ěl dedicated <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[64] On that day the sovereign set apart <dn>את</dn> the middle of the courtyard that was in front of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for there he made ascending offerings, and the grain offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze slaughter-place that was before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was too small to contain <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings, and <dn>את</dn> the fat of the peace offerings.
[65] And Shelomoh at that time performed <dn>את</dn> the Festival, and all Yisra’ěl with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi of Mitsrayim, before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> our <dn>Elohim</dn>, seven days and seven days – fourteen days.
[66] On the eighth day he sent <dn>את</dn> the people away. And they blessed <dn>את</dn> the sovereign, and went to their tents rejoicing and glad of heart for all the goodness that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done for <dn>His</dn> servant Daviḏ, and for Yisra’ěl <dn>His</dn> people.

readings.title: Fire from Heaven Consumes the Offerings
readings.subtitle: The esteem of YeHoVaH fills the House, and the people worship and celebrate.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 7:1] And when Shelomoh had ended praying, fire came down from the heavens and consumed the ascending offering and the slaughterings. And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> filled <dn>את</dn> the House.
[2] And the priests were unable to enter the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, because the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had filled <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[3] And all the children of Yisra’ěl saw <dn>את</dn> how the fire came down, and the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> on the House, and they bowed their faces to the ground on the pavement, and did obeisance and gave thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “For <dn>He</dn> is good, for <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is everlasting.”
[4] And the sovereign and all the people slaughtered slaughterings before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[5] And Sovereign Shelomoh slaughtered <dn>את</dn> a slaughtering of twenty-two thousand bulls and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the sovereign and all the people dedicated <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[6] And the priests were standing over their duties, and the Lěvites with instruments of the song to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which Sovereign Daviḏ had made to give thanks to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “For <dn>His</dn> loving-commitment is everlasting,” whenever Daviḏ praised by their hand. And the priests were blowing trumpets before them, and all Yisra’ěl were standing.
[7] And Shelomoh set apart <dn>את</dn> the middle of the courtyard that was in front of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for there he made ascending offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze slaughter-place which Shelomoh had made was not able to contain <dn>את</dn> the ascending offerings and <dn>את</dn> the grain offerings and <dn>את</dn> the fat.
[8] And Shelomoh at that time observed <dn>את</dn> the Festival seven days, and all Yisra’ěl with him, a very great assembly from the entrance of Ḥamath to the wadi of Mitsrayim.
[9] And on the eighth day they held an assembly, for they performed the dedication of the slaughter-place seven days, and the festival seven days.
[10] And on the twenty-third day of the seventh new moon he sent <dn>את</dn> the people away to their tents, rejoicing and glad of heart for the goodness that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had done for Daviḏ, and for Shelomoh, and for <dn>His</dn> people Yisra’ěl.

readings.title: YeHoVaH's Second Appearance to Shelomoh
readings.subtitle: A covenant of promise and warning is given concerning the Temple and Yisra’ěl.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 9:1] And it came to be, when Shelomoh had finished building <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign, and <dn>את</dn> all the desire of Shelomoh which he was pleased to do,
[2] that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh the second time, as <dn>He</dn> had appeared to him at Gib‛on.
[3] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> your prayer and <dn>את</dn> your supplication that you have made before <dn>Me</dn>. <dn>I</dn> have set <dn>את</dn> this house apart which you have built to put <dn>My</dn> Name there forever, and <dn>My</dn> eyes and <dn>My</dn> heart shall always be there.</dq>
[4] <dq>“And you, if you walk before <dn>Me</dn> as your father Daviḏ walked, in integrity of heart and in uprightness, to do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, if you guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> right-rulings,</dq>
[5] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of your reign over Yisra’ěl forever, as <dn>I</dn> promised Daviḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours on the throne of Yisra’ěl.’</dq>
[6] <dq>“If you at all turn back, you or your sons, from following <dn>Me</dn>, and do not guard <dn>My</dn> commands, <dn>My</dn> laws, which <dn>I</dn> have set before you, but shall go and serve other mighty ones and bow yourselves to them,</dq>
[7] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall cut off <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl from the face of the soil which <dn>I</dn> have given them, and send away from <dn>My</dn> presence <dn>את</dn> this house which <dn>I</dn> have set apart for <dn>My</dn> Name. And Yisra’ěl shall be a proverb and a mockery among all the peoples.</dq>
[8] <dq>“And this house, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and hiss, and say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done thus to this land and to this house?’</dq>
[9] <dq>“Then they shall say, ‘Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> their <dn>Elohim</dn>, who brought their fathers out of the land of Mitsrayim, and they took hold of other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to them and served them. That is why <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has brought all this evil on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Covenant Confirmed
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH hears Shelomoh's prayer and establishes the conditions for blessing and curse.
readings.text:
[2 Chronicles 7:11] Thus Shelomoh finished <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign’s house. And all that came into the heart of Shelomoh to do in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and in his own house, he prosperously executed.
[12] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Shelomoh by night, and said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have heard <dn>את</dn> your prayer, and have chosen this place for <dn>Myself</dn> as a house of slaughtering.</dq>
[13] <dq>“If <dn>I</dn> shut up the heavens and there is no rain, or if <dn>I</dn> command the locusts to devour the land, or if <dn>I</dn> send pestilence among <dn>My</dn> people,</dq>
[14] <dq>and <dn>My</dn> people upon whom <dn>My</dn> Name is called, shall humble themselves, and pray and seek <dn>My</dn> face, and turn from their evil ways, then <dn>I</dn> shall hear from the heavens, and forgive their sin and heal <dn>את</dn> their land.</dq>
[15] <dq>“Now, <dn>My</dn> eyes are open and <dn>My</dn> ears attentive to the prayer of this place.</dq>
[16] <dq>“And now, <dn>I</dn> have chosen and set <dn>את</dn> this house apart for <dn>My</dn> Name to be there forever. And <dn>My</dn> eyes and <dn>My</dn> heart shall always be there.</dq>
[17] <dq>“And you, if you walk before <dn>Me</dn> as your father Daviḏ walked, and do according to all that <dn>I</dn> have commanded you, and if you guard <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> right-rulings,</dq>
[18] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>את</dn> the throne of your reign, as <dn>I</dn> covenanted with Daviḏ your father, saying, ‘There is not to cease a man of yours as ruler in Yisra’ěl.’</dq>
[19] <dq>“But if you turn away and forsake <dn>My</dn> laws and <dn>My</dn> commands which <dn>I</dn> have set before you, and shall go and serve other mighty ones, and bow yourself to them,</dq>
[20] <dq>then <dn>I</dn> shall pluck them from <dn>My</dn> land, which <dn>I</dn> have given them, and this house which <dn>I</dn> have set apart for <dn>My</dn> Name <dn>I</dn> shall cast out of <dn>My</dn> sight and make it to be a proverb and a mockery among all peoples.</dq>
[21] <dq>“And this house, which has been exalted, everyone who passes by it is shall be astonished and say, ‘Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> done thus to this land and this house?’</dq>
[22] <dq>“Then they shall say, ‘Because they forsook <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Mitsrayim, and embraced other mighty ones, and bowed themselves to them and served them, therefore <dn>He</dn> has brought all this evil on them.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Shelomoh's Transaction with Hiram
readings.subtitle: After twenty years of building, Shelomoh gives twenty cities to Hiram in exchange for resources.
readings.text:
[1 Kings 9:10] And it came to be, at the end of twenty years, that Shelomoh had built <dn>את</dn> the two houses, <dn>את</dn> the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and <dn>את</dn> the house of the sovereign.
[11] Ḥiram the sovereign of Tsor had supplied Shelomoh with cedar and cypress and gold, as much as he desired. Then Sovereign Shelomoh gave Ḥiram twenty cities in the land of Galil.
[12] And Ḥiram came from Tsor to see <dn>את</dn> the cities which Shelomoh had given him, but they were not right in his eyes,
[13] and he said, “What are these cities you have given me, my brother?” And he called them the land of Kaḇul, as they are to this day.
[14] And Ḥiram sent the sovereign one hundred and twenty talents of gold.
